surface_mechanism_description: The surface reaction mechanism involves the adsorption of osmocene (OsCp2) and molecular oxygen (O2) on the Al2O3 surface. The OsCp2 precursor decomposes, releasing Os ligands that react with surface hydroxyl groups. The oxygen pulse combusts the remaining ligands, forming an adsorbed oxygen layer. The process is characterized by a nucleation delay, after which the film growth proceeds linearly.
evidence: The noble metals activate O2 by catalyzing its dissociation to adsorbed oxygen atoms, which in turn react with noble metal precursor ligands during the following precursor pulse. The rest of the ligand species of the noble metal precursor are combusted on the surface during the oxygen pulse and adsorbed oxygen layer forms again.
